Colonoscopy (*koloskopi*) is the central diagnostic and monitoring procedure for patients with [[psc|Primær skleroserende kolangitis (PSC)]] within the framework of the Danish national quality database for inflammatory bowel disease (DANIBD). It serves as a key strategy for preventing colorectal cancer, which is a severe complication associated with the condition. In this clinical context, the procedure encompasses both colonoscopies with or without biopsies, as well as total colonoscopies performed by specialist practitioners in both hospital and private practice settings.

The procedure is formally tracked through [[indikator-7|Indikator 7]], which monitors the proportion of patients receiving systematic follow-up. The specific quality target for this indicator requires that at least 80% of adult PSC patients undergo a colonoscopy within an 18-month period [^src1]. On a national level, this development target has been successfully met, with 81% of PSC patients receiving a colonoscopy within the required 18-month timeframe [^src1]. These metrics function as an integrated part of the database's evaluative section, linking clinical evidence and operational quality measurements to ensure equitable, evidence-based treatment across regions and departments.

- Page 34: "Opfølgningen kan foretages af hospital og i speciallægepraksis, hvorfor koloskopi omfatter koloskopi med/uden biopsi samt totale koloskopier foretaget hos praktiserende speciallæger (SKS-koder: KUJF32/35 og ydelseskode: 2114 for specialet ’kirurgi’)." [^src1]
